description.value: The study examined whether anodal tDCS over the left inferior frontal gyrus, combined with language therapy, altered resting-state functional connectivity and whether connectivity changes related to improvements in written naming in people with primary progressive aphasia.

spans.text: In the present study, we examined changes in functional connectivity in the language network, as identified in task-based fMRI studies of spoken and written word production, to determine whether functional connectivity change is a mechanism for tDCS effects in PPA.

design.value: This is an analysis of the first phase results of a larger double-blinded, within-subject crossover clinical trial, analyzed here as a between-subject comparison of participants initially assigned to tDCS versus sham. Both groups received language therapy, with MRI and behavioral data collected before and immediately after treatment.

spans.text: This is an analysis of the first phase results of the current clinical trial, focusing on the association between gains in written naming (the primary outcome measure) and changes in connectivity in participants who initially received tDCS versus those who initially received sham.
